project_name: Core Scientific AUBix Auburn Data Center
status_detail: Core Scientific announced a $135M initial investment, expected $400M total investment, to establish HPC operations in the existing AUBix data center on West Samford Avenue; a 2026 local report says a $55M building permit funds expansion/cooling work and staffing growth.
notes: City of Auburn source gives 16 MW launch capacity and investment. Local news adds 2026 permit/expansion detail.

developer: Unknown; LBYD Incorporated listed as engineering firm
status_detail: Auburn City Council approved a 65,700 sq ft data center on 52 acres at 406 West Veterans Boulevard in Auburn Technology Park; construction timeline and end user were not disclosed in available reporting.
notes: Official packet search result references Conditional Use - Mill Creek Data Center; project specifics are from DCD/Opelika-Auburn News reporting.

status_detail: No verified data center project found in county/EDA/news search.
notes: LCEDA target industries list automotive, advanced manufacturing, aerospace, biotechnology and robotics, not data centers. Athens City Council April 27, 2026 minutes discuss data center zoning as a future conditional use and state neither the Council nor City had considered or planned a data center within city limits; rumors outside city limits were not tied to a verifiable project.

status_detail: Proposed hyperscale data center campus in Lowndes County, about six miles southwest of Montgomery; public materials/news describe roughly 800 acres near Highway 80 and Highway 21, with county leaders/residents still debating and no final decision reported.
notes: LCEDC page identifies Project Red Clay as proposed and Cloverleaf as developer. Capacity estimate from tracker/community-source materials; treat as unconfirmed until permitting/utility filings are available.

status_detail: No verified Macon County data center project found in county/EDA/news search.
notes: County news mentions Meta's Montgomery data center only as part of a state report, while Macon County's highlighted project is Republic Airways LIFT Academy. MCEDA target/featured sites emphasize logistics, aerospace, automotive/manufacturing and CSX/REAL Park opportunities; no Macon data center project located.

status_detail: Meta lists Huntsville as a U.S. data center location with $1.5B+ investment, 2018 groundbreaking and 300+ operational jobs supported once completed; 2022 expansion added two buildings to reach nearly 3.5M sq ft.
notes: Official Meta sources do not disclose MW capacity; third-party trackers often estimate Huntsville market capacity separately.

status_detail: DC BLOX opened its Huntsville data center in 2018 at 333 Diamond Drive NW near Redstone Arsenal; company location page lists the facility as an active Huntsville data center.
notes: MW value from dcmap tracker; DC BLOX official pages verify location and operational status but not capacity.

aliases: Simple Helix Tier III Data Center
status_detail: Simple Helix operates a locally owned data center at 165 West Park Loop NW, Huntsville; 2017 opening announcement described a Tier III enterprise-class facility with two data halls and 1.1 MW total power capacity.
notes: Official company site verifies current Huntsville facility; capacity from company PR/DCD opening coverage.

status_detail: Local reporting and public forums describe a proposed data center affecting Hale and Marengo counties, with residents invited to meetings in Demopolis/Gallion; no developer, formal application, capacity or official project page was found.
notes: Treat as early/low-detail lead. Evidence is local news/community meetings and a petition; no county/EDA or developer source located during this pass.

status_detail: Stream Data Centers states it is unable to proceed with the Marion County site because utility power cannot be sourced within the required timeframe, and Project Liberty will not move forward.
notes: Developer page is direct evidence for the canceled/not-moving-forward status. County EDA page checked for local context.

status_detail: No verified Marshall County data center project found in county/EDA/news search.
notes: Search results around a 540,000 sq ft facility refer to JST's advanced manufacturing/electronic connector project in Guntersville, not a data center. Guntersville/Marshall EDC pages reviewed; no data center project identified.

status_detail: Beacon describes a planned next-generation data center development in Calvert, Mobile County: 95 acres developed within a 650-acre site between Highway 43 and Shepard House Road, two data center buildings, first building targeted for completion in 2027, and current planning/engineering/community engagement phase.
notes: Beacon states initial construction cost is estimated at $6B, closed-loop/no evaporative cooling, 7,500 gallons/day water and sewer use, 1,000 construction jobs and 250 permanent operational jobs.

status_detail: Colocation/data center listings identify Lumen Mobile 1 at 50 North Lawrence Street in Mobile, with about 5,100-5,625 sq ft total space and 1,829 sq ft raised floor/colocation space.
notes: Lumen official colocation page verifies service offering generally but the specific Mobile facility details come from data center directories.

aliases: Regional First Tier III+ Commercial Data Center
status_detail: Mobile Chamber publication describes a regional Tier III+ commercial data center serving customers across Alabama and other Gulf/Southeast states; later trackers list Assurance Technology LLP as an operational Mobile data center provider.
notes: Original source is an older Mobile Chamber PDF advertisement/business publication; exact address/capacity not verified in this pass.

status_detail: No verified Monroe County, Alabama data center project found in county/EDA/news search.
notes: MMCEDA site lists distribution, wood products, metalworking, aerospace and chemical target industries and no data center project. Search results for Monroe County data centers primarily referred to Monroe County, Georgia or other states, not Monroe County, Alabama.
